around.headline: Two-wheeler ban on Airport Road and Electronics City flyovers put on hold, restrictions to be phased in instead
around.summary: Bengaluru traffic police have paused the planned two-wheeler ban on the Airport Road and Electronics City elevated corridors and will phase in vehicle restrictions instead, per Deccan Herald, The Times of India and The Hindu. If you ride a two-wheeler on either corridor, you can keep using it for now, but watch for updated rules as the phase-in rolls out.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Pink Line confirmed ready for a September launch on the Bannerghatta Road stretch
around.summary: BMRCL says the Pink Line's Bannerghatta Road corridor is ready for launch this month, per constructionworld.in. Worth checking BMRCL's announcements soon if your commute currently detours around that stretch.

around.headline: BMTC to share real-time bus tracking with Ola and Uber; NCMC common mobility card coming by month-end
around.summary: BMTC plans to share live bus-location data with ride-hailing apps and launch its NCMC common mobility card by the end of September, alongside a new tool to plan a single bus-auto-cab journey in one shot, per Deccan Herald, Moneycontrol and The Times of India. Could make combining a bus leg with an app-booked auto or cab noticeably easier once it's live.
around.source: Deccan Herald, Moneycontrol, The Times of India

around.headline: Karnataka to move Supreme Court against CWRC order to release more Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu amid drought
around.summary: Karnataka plans to challenge in the Supreme Court a Cauvery Water Regulation Committee order directing it to release more water to Tamil Nadu despite the state's own drought conditions, with the matter listed for a further hearing on September 15, per The Times of India. Watch for any water-supply or usage advisories in the city if the dispute drags on.

around.headline: Geological Survey of India flags TBM shaft site near Lalbagh for Bengaluru's proposed Tunnel Road
around.summary: GSI has raised concerns over a tunnel-boring-machine shaft location planned near Lalbagh for the city's proposed Tunnel Road project, per The Times of India. If you live or work near Lalbagh, this is one to watch for possible construction disruption in the area.

around.headline: Oil prices push back toward $100 a barrel
around.summary: Crude oil prices are once again approaching the $100-a-barrel mark, per oilprice.com, extending a climb that has already been rattling Indian markets. A sustained rise at these levels tends to feed into pump prices and cab/auto fares over the following weeks.

street_smart.title: You're buying vegetables at a busy Bengaluru wholesale market and notice a boy who looks about 12 hauling heavy sacks for one of the shopkeepers — clearly working, not just visiting. He looks uneasy when he catches you looking. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Times of India and other outlets, Sept 8-9 — after Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar visited Yeshwanthpur APMC market and the public flagged child labour on the spot, five police-and-labour teams rescued 19 child labourers (mostly teens from Bihar, West Bengal, UP, Rajasthan and Karnataka) from shops there within hours, with cases registered against the shop owners under the Child Labour and Juvenile Justice Acts. This bystander-notices-child-labour mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The shopkeeper is watching you count your change, not paying attention to the boy. You have a few minutes before you need to move on.

choices.text: Note the shop's name or stall number and a rough description, then once you're clear of the shop call Childline (1098) or report it to the local police/labour inspector — without confronting the shopkeeper directly.
choices.feedback: Correct. This is exactly how yesterday's rescue happened — a tip-off from the public led to a coordinated police-and-labour operation that freed 19 children in hours. Reporting to the right authority lets trained teams act with legal power (and often follow-up protection for the child) that you can't provide on your own, and doing it after you've moved on avoids tipping off the shopkeeper before help arrives.

choices.text: Ignore it — market work is common for teenagers in India anyway, so it's probably fine.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. 'Common' isn't the same as legal or safe: employing a child under 14 in any work, or an adolescent aged 14-18 in hazardous work, is illegal under the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act. Children trafficked from other states are routinely hidden in plain sight at exactly this kind of market — which is why yesterday's rescued children had been brought in from as far as Bihar and West Bengal.

choices.text: Confront the shopkeeper on the spot and demand he let the child go.
choices.feedback: Risky. A direct confrontation can make the shopkeeper hide or relocate the child before any real help arrives, and it puts you in a personal dispute with no lasting protection for the child — the shopkeeper can simply wait you out and put the child back to work once you've left.

choices.text: Take a photo or video of the child working and post it on social media to pressure the market authorities.
choices.feedback: Risky. Publicly posting an identifiable photo of a minor raises its own legal and ethical problems under child-protection law, and it still tips off the shop before an actual rescue team can act. A report to Childline or the police achieves the same pressure with legal authority and without exposing the child online.

takeaways: Call Childline on 1098 (free, 24x7, nationwide) or your local police/labour department if you spot a child clearly working rather than accompanying family — don't confront the employer yourself.

Under the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, employing a child under 14 in any work, or a 14-18-year-old in hazardous work, is illegal; shop owners can be booked and children referred to the Child Welfare Committee.

Avoid photographing or posting images of the child publicly — Indian child-protection law restricts identifying minors, and a report to authorities is both safer for the child and more likely to lead to an actual rescue.

quiz.question: Which Bengaluru Metro line was confirmed ready for a September launch on its Bannerghatta Road stretch?
quiz.why: The Pink Line's Bannerghatta Road stretch needed a BMRCL rolling-stock clearance before trains could run there, which came through earlier this month.

quiz.question: How many child labourers were rescued from Bengaluru's Yeshwanthpur APMC market after CM D.K. Shivakumar's visit prompted a police-and-labour operation?
quiz.why: The 19 rescued children, mostly teenagers, had been brought in from as far as Bihar and West Bengal, and shop owners now face cases under the Child Labour and Juvenile Justice Acts.

quiz.question: Karnataka said it would move the Supreme Court after which committee ordered it to release more Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu amid drought?
quiz.why: The CWRC issues short-term (roughly 15-day) release directions under the broader Cauvery Water Management Authority framework, which is why the dispute keeps resurfacing through the year.

quiz.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes 'untouchability' in any form?
quiz.why: Article 17 not only abolishes untouchability but also makes its practice in any form a punishable offence — one of the few fundamental rights enforceable directly against private individuals, not just the state.

quiz.question: In economics, what term describes a sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services?
quiz.why: Inflation erodes purchasing power over time, which is why a sustained oil-price rise (like today's move back toward $100 a barrel) worries policymakers well beyond just pump prices.
